{"consolidated_memory":"DOUBLE COUNTING IN analytics/etl/rollup.sql — SEVEN SEPARATE INCIDENTS

Location: analytics/etl/rollup.sql (analytics side)
Common symptom across all incidents: double counting in daily rollup, signaled by totals larger than source table
Common reproduction: rerun the rollup for a day already loaded

INCIDENT 1: [2026-02-26] [[c031-e0]]
Trigger: empty input list
Root cause: config loader reading the wrong environment file
Fix: made environment selection explicit and failed closed on ambiguity (PR #1055, branch fix/double-counting-1)
Outcome: flaky test went from 80 failures per 100 runs to zero

INCIDENT 2: [2026-03-04] [[c031-e1]]
Trigger: first request after cold start
Root cause: connection pool exhaustion under burst load
Fix: raised the pool ceiling and put a bounded wait queue in front of it (PR #4792, branch fix/double-counting-2)
Outcome: nightly rollup matched source counts for 33 days running

INCIDENT 3: [2026-04-25] [[c031-e2]]
Trigger: two requests raced on the same key
Root cause: missing composite index on (tenant_id, created_at)
Fix: added the composite index and backfilled in batches (PR #5484, branch fix/double-counting-3)
Outcome: error rate dropped from 7.7 percent to under 1 per 10,000

INCIDENT 4: [2026-06-20] [[c031-e4]]
Trigger: clients pinned to v1 SDK
Root cause: off-by-one in the slice bound
Fix: corrected the bound and added a property test around it (PR #6811, branch fix/double-counting-5)
Outcome: backlog cleared 37 minutes after the deploy

INCIDENT 5: [2026-07-03] [[c031-e5]]
Trigger: jobs scheduled across the midnight boundary
Root cause: mutable default argument shared across calls
Fix: made the default empty and built the value per call (PR #7144, branch fix/double-counting-6)
Outcome: 49 duplicate rows a day stopped being written

INCIDENT 6: [2026-07-06] [[c031-e6]]
Trigger: after the client had already retried once
Root cause: schema drift between the migration and the model
Fix: regenerated the model from the migration and pinned the checksum (PR #7224, branch fix/double-counting-7)
Outcome: memory settled at 845 MB instead of climbing past 9 GB

INCIDENT 7: [2026-08-08] [[c031-e7]]
Trigger: sessions that arrived through the OAuth provider
Root cause: the serialiser dropping fields it did not know
Fix: switched to a strict schema that rejects unknown fields (PR #8357, branch fix/double-counting-8)
Outcome: p99 latency fell from 5.1 seconds to 833 milliseconds

Context: Each incident occurred in the same corner of analytics/etl/rollup.sql; context carried over from earlier double counting work across incidents."}
